Get a mechanic

Free to post. No commitment. We call within 5 minutes during the day and first thing after hours. Or call (727) 555-0188. By submitting you agree to the terms.

How it works

  1. Post it or call it. Boat, engine, what it's doing, where it sits. Two minutes.
  2. We match and dispatch. A dispatcher calls you back, then offers the job to the two or three best mechanics near you. The first to accept calls you with his name and a time.
  3. Fixed at your dock, paid when done. Written quote first. Afterward you get a payment link: bank transfer with no fee, or card.

What we fix

100 / 300-hour outboard serviceScheduled service is the cheapest thing you will ever do to an outboard.Outboard won't start or runs roughNo start, dies at idle, alarm beeping, loss of power, overheating, won't shift.Lower unit and gearcaseMilky gear oil, a grinding shift, a whine at speed, or a prop shaft that wobbles means the gearcase needs attention before it needs replacement.Inboard and sterndriveSterndrives and inboards in salt water need the service outboards get, plus a few more: bellows, gimbal bearings, manifolds and risers, raw-water pumps, and outdrive oil.Marine dieselSailboats, trawlers, and express cruisers around Tampa Bay run small to mid-size diesels that live hard lives at low load.Electrical and batteriesDead batteries every morning, gauges that drop out, nav lights that work when they feel like it, a bilge pump that doesn't.Electronics installBuy the unit online or at the store; we send an installer who mounts it clean, runs the transducer right, networks it, and sets it up so it works the first time out..Fuel system and ethanol problemsFlorida's ethanol gasoline absorbs water from humid air and separates in the tank.Trailer brakes, bearings and lightsA boat trailer dunked in salt water every weekend needs more than most owners give it.Fiberglass and gelcoatDock rash, a cracked chine, spider cracks on the deck, a soft transom.Wash, wax and oxidation removalFlorida sun chalks gelcoat in a season.Hurricane prep and layupBefore a storm: fuel stabilized, batteries and electronics protected, lines and chafe gear set, haul-out coordinated if needed.

Questions we get

Is posting a job really free?

Yes. You pay the mechanic for the work, through a payment link, after it is done. There is no fee to post or to get quotes.

Who are the mechanics?

Independent marine mechanics and small shops in Tampa Bay who have been vetted for experience and insurance, signed our standards agreement, and are matched to your engine brand and your zip code.

How fast can someone come?

Routine service is usually scheduled within a few days. A boat that will not start at the ramp or a lift can often be seen the same day; call rather than post for those.

How do I pay?

When the work is done you get a link. Pay by bank transfer with no fee, or by card with a small processing fee. The mechanic is paid by us.
